enriched_description: Small Old World monkey measuring 30-60 cm body length weighing 2-8 kg. Body covered with long hair around face forming distinctive facial ruff. Fur coloration variable by species in gray, brown, olive, or red. Face bare with expressive features. Eyes forward-facing with brown irises. Nose narrow. Ears small. Tail long and non-prehensile. Hind limbs elongated. Body slender and agile. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. African arboreal monkey with complex social behavior.

Old World monkey measuring 50-85 cm body length weighing 7-13 kg. Body covered with reddish-brown fur with white underparts. Face dark with distinctive white mustache and cheek markings. Eyes forward-facing. Ears small. Tail long and non-prehensile. Limbs exceptionally long relative to body size adapted for terrestrial running. Body slender and athletic. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Fastest primate capable of 55 km/h. West African savanna dweller.

Large Old World monkey measuring 50-115 cm body length weighing 14-40 kg. Body covered with olive-brown to gray fur. Face elongated with doglike muzzle and prominent jaws. Eyes forward-facing with brown irises. Ears small. Tail moderate length. Body robust and muscular. Ischial callosities (sitting pads) bare and calloused. Males significantly larger than females with prominent canine teeth. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Terrestrial ground-dwelling monkey of Africa.

Old World monkey measuring 40-70 cm body length weighing 5-15 kg. Body covered with brown, gray, or black fur. Face bare and pink to dark in coloration. Eyes forward-facing with brown irises. Nose prominent. Ears small. Tail moderate to long length. Body stocky and muscular. Ischial callosities present. Cheek pouches for food storage. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Monkey of rocky regions of Asia and Africa. Highly adaptable and opportunistic.

Old World monkey measuring 50-75 cm body length weighing 8-20 kg. Body covered with gray, black, or golden fur. Face bare and black with prominent brow ridges. Eyes forward-facing. Ears small and framed by fur ruff. Tail extremely long (exceeding body length) and non-prehensile. Body slender with elongated limbs. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Slender long-tailed monkey of Asia. Arboreal with leaf-eating specialization and complex stomach.

Old World monkey measuring 45-75 cm body length weighing 4-14 kg. Body covered with long silky fur in black, white, or brown with contrasting mantle pattern. Face bare and black framed by white fur ruff. Eyes forward-facing. Ears small. Tail long and non-prehensile. Thumbs reduced or absent (name derives from Greek 'kolobos' meaning mutilated). Body slender. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Arboreal monkey of western and central Africa. Folivorous with sacculated stomach.

Old World monkey measuring 55-75 cm body length weighing 7-24 kg. Body covered with reddish-brown fur with lighter underparts. Males possess extraordinarily long bulbous nose (proboscis) hanging over mouth. Face bare and pinkish. Eyes forward-facing. Ears small. Tail long and non-prehensile. Body pot-bellied with enlarged digestive system. Males significantly larger than females. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Borneo endemic with aquatic adaptations including webbed feet.

Small New World monkey measuring 15-28 cm body length weighing 100-500 g. Body covered with soft fur in variable coloration including white, black, brown, or orange. Face bare with distinctive white ear tufts in some species. Eyes forward-facing with brown irises. Nose flat. Ears often tufted. Tail long and non-prehensile with ringed pattern. Claws instead of nails on most digits (except big toe). Body tiny and agile. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Smallest monkey of South and Central America.

New World monkey measuring 30-55 cm body length weighing 1.5-5 kg. Body covered with brown, black, or white fur. Head bears thick cap of dark hair resembling monk's cowl. Face bare and pinkish. Eyes forward-facing with brown irises. Nose flat. Ears small. Tail long and prehensile with bare tactile patch on underside. Body medium-sized and robust. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Highly intelligent monkey of Central and South America. Tool-using capability.

New World monkey measuring 40-70 cm body length weighing 4-10 kg. Body covered with thick black, brown, or reddish fur. Face bare and black. Eyes forward-facing. Nose flat. Ears small. Tail long and fully prehensile with bare tactile tip. Body robust with enlarged hyoid bone in males producing loud howling calls audible 5 km. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Monkey of tropical South American forests. Loudest land animal relative to size.
